title: Virtual Reality Versus Traditional Exercise on EMG Activity in Postural Malalignment
official: Influence of Virtual Reality Versus Traditional Exercise on Trapezius Muscle EMG Activity in Relaxed and Corrected Postures Among Individuals With and Without Postural Malalignment
summary: This study aims to investigate the immediate effects of virtual reality (VR)-based exercise compared with traditional Active free exercise on trapezius muscle activation in adults with and without postural malalignment. Surface electromyography (EMG) will be used to assess upper, middle, and lower trapezius muscle activity during relaxed and corrected postures and during VR and traditional exercise. Demographic data will be collected. The study will also assess posture, trapezius muscle strength, cervical range of motion, Activity level, craniovertebral angle, and neck proprioception. Approximately 40 adults aged 18-35 years will participate in a single study session. The findings may help determine whether VR-based rehabilitation provides an effective and engaging approach for assessing and training postural control and trapezius muscle activation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

participants will include healthy individuals or individuals with postural malalignment.

* Age 18-35 years
* Able to provide written informed consent
* Able to stand and perform light movement tasks safely
* Normal or corrected-to-normal vision
* Sufficient intellectual ability to understand and follow instructions
* Basic English proficiency to understand study instructions and questionnaires
* For symptomatic participants, presence of postural dysfunction at baseline, including one or more of the following:
* Forward head posture
* Rounded shoulder posture

Exclusion Criteria:

* \- Epilepsy
* Severe balance disorders
* Major neurological or musculoskeletal conditions
* Recent injuries
* Use of medications affecting balance
* Pregnancy
